children: The National Stock Exchange has tightened compliance norms for retail algorithmic trading, reiterating that static IP access is strictly restricted to individual investors who develop their own trading algorithms using programming knowledge.

In a circular issued by its Inspection Department on Friday, November 20, titled 'Compliance with the guidelines on 'Safer participation of Retail investors in Algorithmic trading' issued by SEBI and Exchanges – Tech-savvy Retail Investors', the exchange directed trading members and algo providers not to grant static IP access under any circumstances to retail clients who do not fall under the "tech-savvy retail investor" category. The directive took effect immediately.

The move reinforces the regulatory framework established by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in February 2025 and subsequent exchange guidelines issued in July 2025, which came into force across stockbrokers on April 1, 2026.
Under those norms, only retail traders who code their own strategies are eligible to execute trades via broker application programming interfaces (APIs) mapped to a whitelisted static IP.

By contrast, retail clients who use ready-made algorithms or strategies built by third-party vendors must execute them through exchange-empanelled algo providers, with all strategies hosted on brokers' servers so that order messages originate directly from the broker's infrastructure.
According to the NSE circular, this requirement is central to preserving the broker's control over risk management and safeguarding data confidentiality.
To enforce adherence, the NSE has prescribed monetary penalties for brokers that fail to obtain the mandatory undertaking from tech-savvy retail clients before enabling static IP algo access.

Non-compliant trading members will face a penalty of ₹5,000 per client, capped at ₹1 lakh on the first instance, with the fine escalating by 50% on the second violation and by 100% from the third violation onwards.
For empanelled algo providers, any breach of the static IP restriction will trigger a review of their empanelment status, which may be suspended or revoked by the exchange.

title: NSE tightens retail algo trading compliance, restricts static IP access to self-coding investors
